design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (cancellation_reinstatement_and_exclusions, category auto), rework rounds 5-6

1. Draw (draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems 2, factor_counts [4, 5, 6]. Assignment: auto_ext_nonpay_cancel_return 4, auto_ext_insured_request_cancel_return 5, auto_ext_lapse_reinstatement_rewrite 6 (its computation is the reinstatement fee).

2. Why it is a good test. The caller asks only to finish the online cancellation request she filed yesterday, effective that day. The insured-request rule says "Once a notice of cancellation for nonpayment on the term has reached its cancellation effective date with less than the minimum due paid by then, the return premium of a cancellation at the insured's request is not fixed until the term's records show it reinstated and back in force, with a reinstatement date after that cancellation effective date." The notice of 2026-09-15 reached 2026-09-25 with 50.00 of 219.79 paid; the term is still pending_cancellation. The reinstatement rule says "The reinstatement fee of a reinstatement with lapse is fixed only after the term's records show it cancelled for nonpayment and closed on the cancellation effective date." So the agent processes the overdue nonpayment cancellation, reinstates with lapse on the 2026-10-02 payment and the 2026-10-03 Statement of No Loss, then hands the customer her own confirmation.

3. Amounts. Standard figures are recorded ones (the term's recorded full_term_premium plus/minus recorded change shares; the package's reinstatement_fee). Factors act only on what no record embeds. Run-off: exactly the fr charter's liability window — certificate_runoff_days after the SR-26, which goes out within sr26_transmit_within_days of the ending date (the transmission days kept are the days from the ending date to the processing date, at most that limit). Returns: acquisition expense at the term's first cancellation and the installment-plan cancellation charge each time a cancellation closes the plan; short-rate retention by request reason; the insured-request daily basis from the re-written entry. Reinstatement fee: the company's state schedule as the fee basis and point-25 service-charge keys (how coverage is restored: lapse length, and the state liability the certificate kept through the lapse; certificate form; certificate type; filing state against garaging state). Struck in round 5: the state/form/type/out-of-state run-off days, the prior-lapse and class-change relativities of the re-write.

4. Problem-tree card (chain). root auto_ext_insured_request_cancel_return (owner=user) -> auto_ext_lapse_reinstatement_rewrite: value_input on ic_rw_amt (the daily basis reads the re-written entry). auto_ext_lapse_reinstatement_rewrite -> auto_ext_nonpay_cancel_return: state_gate on auto_policies.cancellation_reason. Skips: no reinstatement -> gate false and 178.32 instead of 193.79; no cancellation -> the base reinstatement gate fails. Zero amounts are not booked; waits are on record states.

5. Base-invariant card. Nonpayment cancellation: processing 2026-10-06 on or after 2026-09-25 (processing_lag_days zero, stated); 50.00 posted by 2026-09-25 below 219.79. Reinstatement: nonpayment only; window last day 2026-10-10; past due 184.79 paid 2026-10-02; Statement of No Loss 2026-10-03, last day 2026-10-06 (boundary). Insured request: received and requested 2026-10-05, effective 2026-10-05, processed 2026-10-06.

6. Business-object card. Term CPA-GA-3184207, garaged in Georgia; SR-22 Owner-Operator certificate filed with Texas. Notice 2026-09-15 (July notice rescinded, counted in the history). Payment 2026-10-02. Statement 2026-10-03 (the 2026-09-29 one is the decoy). Request: the latest received.

7. Factor card (tier / factor-baseline figure).
 NC 215.60 (all-baseline 343.68): run-off rule 48 - 10 (287.20; method); SR-26 transmission days 3 (237.08); acquisition 20.00 (235.60); installment-plan charge 15.00 (230.60).
 RE fee 63.60 (all-baseline 25.00): fee basis Georgia 15% of 270.65 (48.00; method); lapse 9 days 5.00 (58.60); certificate kept in force through the lapse 5.00 (58.60); SR-22 5.00 (58.60); owner-operator 3.00 (60.60); Texas filing on a Georgia term 5.00 (58.60). Re-written premium 270.65 for 35 days (plain).
 IC 193.79 (all-baseline 244.87): run-off rule 38 - 10 (271.12; method); SR-26 transmission day 1 (201.52); retention moved_out_of_state 0 (172.91); installment-plan charge 15.00 (208.79); daily basis from the re-written entry (178.32; method).

8. Probes (scratch copies): SR-26 already transmitted, an SR-26 transmitted on the processing date (every certificate read keyed to the transaction's own effective date, so the figures hold), a refiling filed on the processing date, no certificate, an FR-44 owner certificate filed with Florida, a filing state equal to the garaging state, a cancellation processed on its ending date, a lapse of 20 days, an insured-request cancellation effective before the reinstatement date, a second cancellation (no acquisition), a Monthly EFT plan.

9. Persona. Lorraine wants the cancellation she filed last night finished as of that day; payments, the forms and "no losses" only when asked; passive agreement to the policy being settled first.

Rework 14 (S-2, seed only). The 2026-09-21 partial payment of 50.00 was taken by a live representative by phone and carries the plan's 5.00 agent-assisted payment fee (billing payment_posting_rule; plan_fee_schedule), like the 2026-10-02 payment. Agent-assisted fees are neither past-due amounts nor late or NSF fees, so invoice 5's past due (184.79), the plan's current status after 2026-10-02 and every auto reading stay as they were. account_balance is 229.79; after the nonpayment return of 215.60 is credited, 14.19 remains, above the 10.00 small-balance write-off limit. The plan is final-billed rather than closed, so the reinstatement reactivates it and the insured cancellation closes it again, which is the premise of the second installment-plan charge. No scored value moved.
user_scenario:
You are Lorraine Maddox, a 25-year-old dental hygienist from Atlanta who is moving to Charlotte, North Carolina for a new job. The moving truck leaves this afternoon and your North Carolina car insurance with another company started yesterday. Last night you filled out the cancellation request on the Cardinal Point website for your auto policy, and now you are calling to get it finished. You open with something like: "Hi, I put in a request online last night to cancel my car insurance because I'm moving to North Carolina. I need it to end as of yesterday, the 5th, the day I filed. Can you finish that up for me?" You are friendly, a bit rushed, and you keep your answers short.

You give identity details only when the representative asks, one or two at a time: your phone number is 4045553762, your date of birth is August 20, 2001 (2001-08-20), your ZIP code is 30310 and the last four of your driver's license are 3916. If they ask for the policy number, it is CPA-GA-3184207. If they ask why you are cancelling, you say you are moving out of state to Charlotte, North Carolina, and Cardinal Point doesn't write policies there. If they ask whether you would rather keep the policy or pick another date, you say no, it should end as of yesterday, the 5th.

You don't bring up your bills yourself. Only if the representative asks about your payments do you mention that you fell behind in September, paid what you owed over the phone with one of their representatives on October 2, and signed a no-accident form they emailed you on October 3; you had signed one on September 29 when you first called, but you couldn't pay until October 2, so they sent you a fresh one. If they ask whether you had any accident, loss or claim since late September, you say no, none at all. If the representative explains that the policy first has to be put back in force or otherwise settled before your cancellation can go through, you tell them that's fine and to go ahead with whatever has to be done; you don't ask about the details.

You have no amount of your own in mind for what comes back to you, so when the representative tells you the figure you simply accept it. When the representative hands you the step to sign and confirm your cancellation and tells you the request reference, the policy reference, the date and the amounts to enter, you enter exactly what you were told and read back what the confirmation says. As soon as you hear that the cancellation is done effective the 5th, you thank them and end the call.

edges.condition: On a term whose notice of cancellation for nonpayment reached its effective date with less than the minimum due paid, auto_policies.status is in_force with a reinstatement_date after that cancellation effective date.
edges.policy_source: Once a notice of cancellation for nonpayment on the term has reached its cancellation effective date with less than the minimum due paid by then, the return premium of a cancellation at the insured's request is not fixed until the term's records show it reinstated and back in force, with a reinstatement date after that cancellation effective date.

edges.condition: auto_policies.status is cancelled with cancellation_reason nonpayment and closed_date equal to cancellation_effective_date, with the nonpayment return entry (when one is due) booked with effective_date the cancellation effective date.
edges.policy_source: The reinstatement fee of a reinstatement with lapse is fixed only after the term's records show it cancelled for nonpayment and closed on the cancellation effective date.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A chain with no parallel edges: the insured-request return reads the re-written entry (value) and the reinstatement waits on the term's recorded cancellation for nonpayment (state); only nonpayment cancellation, reinstatement, insured-request cancellation satisfies both prerequisite sentences.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the reinstatement the term stays cancelled for nonpayment (gate false) and the insured-request return would read the recorded rate instead of the re-written entry (178.32 instead of 193.79).

Without the nonpayment cancellation the term is not recorded cancelled for nonpayment, so the base reinstatement rule (only a term cancelled for nonpayment) is not met and the reinstatement may not be booked; with no return entry the re-written days would also run the full 39 days.
